bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion and a sharply increasing contracted backlog indicate strong customer demand for AI infrastructure. This provides multi-period revenue visibility, supports continued capacity utilization, and strengthens CoreWeave’s position as AI workloads scale.

High adjusted EBITDA margins and improving adjusted operating income suggest that infrastructure scale can translate into stronger operating leverage. If utilization and deployment remain disciplined, this provides a durable pathway toward better profitability as revenue expands.

Growth beyond basic GPU capacity into managed inference and broader platform capabilities can deepen customer integration and diversify revenue. Technical validation and rapid product adoption may improve differentiation as enterprises increasingly deploy production AI workloads.

bear.t: High leverage and rising interest burden
bear.b: Debt materially exceeds equity, leaving limited financial flexibility while interest expense is rising with capacity funding. This can absorb a growing share of operating cash flow, increase refinancing exposure, and constrain investment choices if demand or utilization weakens.

bear.t: Heavy capital spending and negative free cash flow
bear.b: Operating cash generation is currently overwhelmed by the investment required to expand GPU infrastructure. Sustaining growth therefore depends on continued access to financing and successful deployment of assets, increasing execution risk and pressure on long-term cash conversion.

Healthy gross margins and adjusted EBITDA have not yet translated into GAAP profitability, as overhead, depreciation, interest, and other costs remain substantial. Continued losses reduce internally generated capital and make the business more dependent on financing while it scales.
